new_sources.title: A note on complex plane curve singularities up to diffeomorphism and their rigidity
new_sources.publication_note: Research in the Mathematical Sciences 11, article 28 (2024); published 27 March 2024. Only Section 2.1, Definition 2.1 and Theorem 2.3 used for classical ambient topological invariance of smoothness of a plane curve.

complete_pages_visually_checked.content: Definition 2.1: ambient homeomorphism of plane curve germs, including the surrounding scope.
Definition 2.2 and Theorem 2.3: branch value semigroups and embedded topological classification.

actual_external_input.statement: A reduced complex plane curve germ ambiently homeomorphic to a smooth complex line is analytically nonsingular.
actual_external_input.derivation: Theorem 2.3 gives one branch and the semigroup of a smooth branch; Definition 2.2 then gives an order-one holomorphic function along the primitive normalization, forcing a nonzero derivative.
actual_external_input.scope: Complex dimension two inside a genuine actual g stable or unstable leaf. H supplies an ambient homeomorphism within that leaf, not merely an abstract homeomorphism of the curve.
not_used: The paper main theorem about smooth diffeomorphisms
Any regularity of H beyond homeomorphism

internal_inputs: 76 actual compact suspension and marked toral conjugacy
86 actual twisted returns and dense return parameters
87 fixed-side common line on Y minus a proper closed Z
91 identification of that line with the specified topological central fine foliation
proof_checks: Annihilator argument proves every g stable leaf dense, not just existence of a dense orbit.
Continuation into each fixed actual leaf uses complete induced leaf metric and holomorphic defining functions; transverse holomorphicity is never assumed.
A curve is shown central by continuation into every actual stable leaf, discreteness of one nontrivial plane-equality locus on its normalization, and note91.
Area bound uses two generic complex projections and finite zero counts, with constants local to the chosen nonzero intersection equation.
Analytic limits are obtained from bounded-degree monic factors; multiplicities are allowed until reduced supports are taken.
Invariance of domain only gives an analytic branch; ambient topology, rather than the abstract disk property, is used to exclude a cusp.
After all fine leaves are analytic and smooth, a separate degree-one projection argument proves uniform local graphs and continuity of tangents.
not_claimed: Resolution of note76 or general Ghys rigidity
model_checks: Analytical substitutions in notes05 and92; scope comparison with local rough/concentration models11,18,85,88. No old numerical suites rerun.
novelty_status: Classical tools; limited searches do not establish novelty of the specific extension argument.
